title: evaluate_alert must skip when the reloaded detector type no longer matches the queue prepare picked
answers: AI detector alert ran on a worker without model credentials
what happens if alert detector type changes between prepare and evaluate
why did my alert check get skipped after editing the detector
body:
Invariant: CheckAlertWorkflow picks the evaluate task queue during prepare, based on the detector type it read (`EvaluateAlertActivityInputs.uses_llm_detector`). Only the AI worker holds the model credentials. posthog/temporal/alerts/activities.py:evaluate_alert reloads the alert with `_load_alert_for_evaluation`, so a detector-type edit made in between could send the check to a worker that cannot run it.
Enforced in evaluate_alert: if `is_llm_detector_config(alert.detector_config) != inputs.uses_llm_detector`, it logs `alerts.skip_detector_type_changed` and returns `EvaluateAlertResult(alert_check_id=None, should_notify=False, ...)` without writing a check or moving `next_check_at`. The next scheduler tick then prepares and routes the alert again, the same way the fingerprint guard skips.
Also: choose the executor (`_LLM_EVALUATE_EXECUTOR`) from the same snapshot you evaluate. Never re-read the alert after routing.
If you add new routing inputs computed in prepare, re-validate them against the reloaded snapshot the same way. Tests that run evaluate_alert must pass a `uses_llm_detector` that matches the alert's detector_config, or the activity skips.
applies: posthog/temporal/alerts activities that route alert evaluation by detector type
